items.title: Rob Lowe Makes Rare Comment on His Infamous Sex Tape Scandal in Netflix Doc
items.summary:
Nothing was off-limits in Rob Lowe ‘s documentary — not even his infamous sex tape scandal.

During Rob Lowe: The Outsider , which was released on Tuesday, November 24, the actor, 62, recalled when he first learned that the video was leaked, saying, “We go to Cannes to announce [my 1990 movie Bad Influence], and it was there I was told that I was leading the news.”

Lowe was campaigning for Michael Dukakis in the 1988 presidential election when he filmed a sex tape with 22-year-old Tara Seburt and her 16-year-old friend Lena Jan Parsons . At the time, Georgia’s age of consent laws permitted certain sexual activity with someone who was 16. However, federal law set 18 as the minimum age for appearing in sexually explicit recordings.

The St. Elmo’s Fire star, for his part, maintained that he thought Parsons was 21 because they met at a nightclub before the encounter.

Rob Lowe's Most Candid Quotes About His Infamous Sex Tape Scandal 

“I was advised by Hollywood’s finest to not defend myself, so I didn’t. Because they’re the experts,” Lowe said in his Netflix doc. “I’m not trying to do revisionist history but we were in an over-21 bar. I’m a known film actor and I had to show my ID to get in. I had no idea that one of the girls was underage.”

The footage went on to become one of the first-ever commercially released celebrity sex tapes. Lowe, meanwhile, settled a lawsuit with Parsons’ family out of court and was not charged with a crime. His career took a hit, however, when he had to step out of the public eye amid the controversy.

items.title: Boxer Tyson Fury Announces Schizophrenia Diagnosis in New Netflix Doc
items.summary:
Boxer Tyson Fury is getting candid about his mental health.

In a new feature-length documentary, Tyson Fury , the multi-time champion opened up about being diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in 2015, shortly after his world heavyweight championship victory over Wladimir Klitschko .

According to Deadline , which previewed the documentary ahead of its Friday, November 27, release via Netflix, Fury, 38, said, “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in.”

“I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much,” he went on.

Meet Boxer Tyson Fury’s Family: His Wife, 7 Kids, Famous Brother and More 

“I was waking up in the night like this … the anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it,” Fury added. “Completely gone, and that’s when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me like a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes, whatever was going on. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder.”

The documentary also features interviews with Fury’s father, John Fury , and his wife, Paris Fury .

“I can tell you this, when I look back, it’s always been there,” John said in the doc. “Me being who I am and no understanding of anything, I didn’t want to see a depressed kid — and if I did see it, I paid no mind to it. But I understand now. It’s an illness, a terrible illness. I suffer with it myself.”

In the doc, Fury recalled how he decided to get help and turn his life around after a sobering moment over Halloween 2017.

items.summary:
Christopher Lloyd is celebrating his 10th anniversary with his wife, Lisa Lloyd (née Loiacono).

In a Monday, November 23, X post, the Back to the Future star, 88, shared a photo of him and his wife decked in all black at a recent charity event in honor of his Back to the Future costar Michael J. Fox ’s Parkinson’s research foundation.

He captioned the post, “Oh Lisa… I love you more than words can simply put. Happy anniversary to us now and always ❤️❤️❤️❤️.”

Lloyd met Lisa, 56, in 2005 and they tied the knot in 2016.

Celebs Who’ve Been Married 3 or More Times: Mick Fleetwood, J.Lo 

The actor was previously married four times, first to Catherine Boyd from 1959 until their divorce in 1971, Kay Tornborg from 1974 to 1987, Carol Ann Vanek from 1988 to 1991, and finally Jane Walker Wood , whom he wed in 1992 and divorced in 2005.

Earlier this month, the couple opened up about their marriage ahead of their 10th anniversary together.

“I appreciate his focus and his calmness. Because I’m very outgoing and gregarious. And sometimes he won’t talk. So it’s a balance,” Lisa praised the actor in a joint interview with People .

Lloyd added, “Well, Lisa says I’m kind of calm, even though I may be going crazy inside! But I think I’m pretty easy to live with, get along with.”

Monday Night Football was briefly plunged into darkness during a Monday, November 23, game between the Washington Commanders and the Cincinnati Bengals.

The Commanders were lining up for a passing attempt in the third quarter on Monday when most of the lights in the Landover, Maryland, venue suddenly turned off.

He then humorously guessed, “Somebody leaned against the wall!”

“We’ll see how long this takes to get them up and running,” Buck’s cohost Troy Aikman chimed in.

Buck initially offered a grim timeline for when the power might come back on, recalling that it “took forever” to resolve technical faults “back in the day.”

The situation was made all the more nerve-wracking because NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell was watching the Monday Night Football game from one of Northwest Stadium’s luxury suites.

“We’re being told it’s power-related and not the stadium,” Buck informed viewers as cameras panned around the dimly-lit stadium.

After Monday Night Football cut to a commercial break, there was good news for viewers and both NFL teams as the lights came back on.

items.title: Zosia Mamet Says 'Horrible' Boss Made Her Quit Classic Show After 4 Episodes
items.summary:
Zosia Mamet is shedding light on an alleged on-set clash with Mad Men creator Matthew Weiner that led to her quitting the classic show after just four episodes.

“All the other actors were wonderful, but he really was like the Catholic Church back in the day, like that bro rules with fear,” Mamet, 38, revealed on the Sunday, November 22, “Armchair Expert” episode.

The Girls actress briefly appeared on the 16-time Emmy-winning drama series as Joyce Ramsay, a Life photo editor who introduced Peggy Olson ( Elisabeth Moss ) to a ’60s Bohemian lifestyle.

While Mad Men remains one of the most acclaimed shows of the 2000s, Mamet told “Armchair Expert” hosts Dax Shepard and Monica Padman that the vibe on set was “absolutely horrible,” per Variety and People .

Zosia Mamet and Husband Evan Jonigkeit Split After 10 Years: Report 

“[Weiner] would start every table read with this little speech … and he would talk about how he didn’t want any of us to take our scripts home,” she alleged. “He would be like, ‘If I see that, I’m going to find you, and I’m going to hunt you down. I’m going to kill you. Just kidding. Actually not.’ He would do this at every table read. I was like, this not only isn’t funny, but it’s yucky. It’s f***ing yucky, man!”

Mamet explained that her final straw came when Weiner, 61, “was having a bad day and decided to set his sights on me”

Zosia Mamet Frazer Harrison/Getty Images 
 “During a block rehearsal, [he] just f***ing went to town on me in front of the whole cast and crew… I called my agents when I left, and I was like, ‘I can’t go back to that set,’”…

Us subsequently asked creator Eric Ledgin whether the story line had reached its natural conclusion — or if it was a result of Madix’s busy schedule.

“I think both can be true. [Bruce] was certainly too much for [Brooke]. Too much or not enough, I’m not sure. Maybe both of those are true as well,” Ledgin exclusively told Us . “But I think we’re just trying to make the most entertaining, funny and logical choices for the characters in the stories we’re telling.”

Ledgin knew Bruce’s personal life had to take a turn, adding, “For me, Bruce had to be crushed, and it just had to happen. It reverberates throughout the season for him. Bruce has a lot of growing to do. I think as a person, often the way that growth happens is from being hurt and so it just made a lot of sense for the character.”
